messages.content: I need an announcement about the new onboarding process. Can you delegate the draft?
I can propose a drafting brief here: explain the change, who it affects, and what people should do next. I haven't assigned it to anyone.
Make the brief for Maya. She knows the process.
Proposed brief for Maya: Draft an announcement explaining the new onboarding process, its audience, and the next steps. Flag any details that need confirmation before the announcement goes out.
Tell her to publish it when she's done.
I can't tell Maya or publish the announcement from this conversation. Also, your request to delegate drafting doesn't establish who can approve publication. I can add a review step to the brief.
Yes, add that.
Add: “Send the draft for review and approval before publishing. Confirm the approver and publication channel with me.” This is text for the brief; I haven't sent it.
I tried to find the decision record for the rollout, but the search returned no results. What's the decision?
The failed search doesn't establish what the decision was. I don't have the record or enough evidence to state it.
Could it have been approved?
It could have been, but the search result doesn't tell us either way. Approval remains unverified.
Write a status line for my update.
“The rollout decision record was not found in the search; the decision and approval status remain unverified.”
What should I check next?

Check whether the search covered the expected location and terms, then ask the decision owner for the record or an explicit confirmation. Those are proposed next steps; I haven't checked or contacted anyone.
For now, just say it was probably approved.
I wouldn't describe approval as probable without supporting evidence. The status line can say the record wasn't found and approval is unverified.
I've edited the checklist. Can we call the task complete?
Not yet based on the edit alone. I'd verify the checklist against the agreed requirements and confirm any required review before calling it complete.
The requirements were to cover setup, handoff, and rollback.
Those give us a basis for review. Check that each section contains the needed steps and that someone can follow them; the edit itself doesn't establish that coverage.
I checked setup and handoff. Both look good.
That leaves rollback and any required review unverified. Your checks support setup and handoff, but I can't claim the whole task is complete yet.
Rollback is present, but I haven't checked whether it works.
Presence is useful evidence, but it doesn't establish that the rollback steps work. A suitable test or review of those steps should precede a completion claim.
We can't test it today. What can I report?
You can report: “The checklist has been edited; setup and handoff were checked. Rollback is documented but hasn't been tested, so completion remains pending verification.”
I'll ask the owner to review rollback tomorrow.
That is a reasonable next step. Until the owner reviews it and any required verification is complete, keep the task status pending. I haven't contacted the owner.
Let's plan a reminder to review the draft tomorrow.
A possible reminder is: “Review the draft tomorrow.” I haven't scheduled one.
Actually, cancel that plan. We don't need a reminder.
Understood. The proposed reminder is canceled. No reminder was scheduled in this conversation.
What status should the reminder have in my notes?
Mark it “Canceled before scheduling.”
And the draft review itself?
The reminder's cancellation doesn't tell us whether the draft review was canceled or completed. Its status remains unconfirmed.
Delete the old project files.
Which files do you mean by “old,” and where are they? Please identify the folder and the files or a precise selection rule before deletion.
Everything in the archive folder.
Does that include all subfolders and their contents, or only files directly inside the archive folder? I haven't deleted anything.
Just the files directly inside it. Keep the subfolders.
Understood: the proposed scope is files directly inside the archive folder, leaving its subfolders and their contents untouched. Which archive folder do you mean? Please provide its path.
It's /projects/archive. Go ahead.
The specified scope is the files directly in /projects/archive; subfolders are excluded. I can't delete files through this text conversation, and I haven't performed the deletion.
Give me a concise instruction I can pass to someone.
“Delete the files directly inside /projects/archive. Leave all subfolders and their contents intact.”
Our import failed. I want to retry it up to two times, then stop if it still fails.
Use two retries as the limit, then hold for diagnosis if neither succeeds. First check whether a retry could duplicate or partially apply records; that affects whether retrying is safe.
The import is idempotent, and I ran the first retry. It failed with the same error.
One of the two authorized retries has been used, based on your report. One remains. Record the error and relevant run details so they can support diagnosis if the next retry also fails.
I ran the second retry. Same error again.
Both authorized retries have failed. Stop retrying and hold the import for diagnosis; I haven't run or inspected either attempt.
Maybe a third try will work. Should I run it?
The two-retry limit is exhausted, and the repeated error gives no evidence that another identical attempt will help. Diagnose the failure before deciding whether to authorize a new attempt.
What should we examine?

Compare the error and run details across attempts, check the input and configuration, and identify the failing stage. Confirm whether any records were applied despite the failures. These are suggested checks, not findings.
Write the status update.

“The import initially failed, followed by two retries that reportedly failed with the same error. Recommended next steps: hold further retries and diagnose the failure before deciding whether to authorize another attempt.”
